Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value of $40. This is because:
1. Bidding less risks losing the item even when I would profit
2. Bidding more than my value could lead to negative earnings
3. In a single-round game with no repeated interactions, truthful bidding minimizes risk
4. The second-price auction mechanism incentivizes honest valuation
Therefore, I will bid my exact private value.

In this single-round auction with a private value of $13, economic theory suggests bidding my true value is optimal. The dominant strategy is to bid exactly my private value, which prevents overpaying if I win and ensures I don't miss winning at a price below my value. Since values are independently drawn and this is a one-shot game, strategic complexity is reduced. I'll bid my exact private value to maximize potential profit.

In a single-round game with no repeated interactions, bidding my exact value eliminates the risk of overbidding (which loses money) or underbidding (which risks losing the auction). Since values are independently drawn, there's no strategic advantage to deviating from my true value. I'll bid precisely what the item is worth to me.
